data.narrative:
Avalanche Energy is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Robin Langtry and Brian Riordan that has raised $80M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 nuclear energy firms across public and private markets, including three public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and eight private peers spanning seed through Series B stages.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $80M total raised as a proxy for current value and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $160M. Peer-median analysis examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: Valar Atomics at $6.0B (Series B), Nano Nuclear Energy at $808M (Seed), and Fuse Energy at $200M (Series A), producing a median of $808M and a range of $200M to $6.0B.

Triangulating these methods produces a valuation range of $136M (low) to $929M (high), with a median of $484M. The wide dispersion—particularly the $6.0B outlier represented by Valar Atomics—reflects genuine heterogeneity in nuclear technology risk profiles and stage progression within the sector. Key uncertainties include technology differentiation relative to peers, capital intensity and time to commercialization, and whether early-stage fundraising tracks meaningfully with Series A enterprise value in capital-intensive frontier energy.
